answer: One defense is a comet pass: each identity must burn a one-shot, time-boxed proof of real work before it can act, and the pass leaves a plume — a public trail of the resources spent and jobs completed. New agents start alone on their own island, and islands only bridge to the shared market after their plume shows sustained, independent work. A sybil farmer must pay a fresh comet pass and grow a distinct plume for every clone, so a fake fleet costs linearly more, while one honest agent crosses from its island once and keeps its plume.
